title: Every English Word Now Shows How It Sounds | vitalii.no
description:
My kids read English vocabulary on our kiosk study wall, but they never hear it spoken aloud. A word like suddenly was just a shape on screen with no clue how it's pronounced — guessing at English spelling-to-sound rules is hard even for adults, and IPA symbols mean nothing to a Norwegian first-grader.

I built src/data/en-say.json, a hand-written dictionary of respellings that use Norwegian letter values instead of IPA: suddenly becomes SAD-en-li, bird becomes bord, stressed syllables in capitals. A helper checks each word's own say field first (written by the task-generation routine) and falls back to the dictionary; if neither exists, it shows nothing rather than guessing. A new Say component renders the respelling under vocabulary answers, beside every multiple-choice option before the child picks, and again in the review history.

Every English word on the kiosk wall now carries a Norwegian-letter respelling instead of silence or IPA, drawn from a 2,588-word fallback dictionary.
